items.title: Gemma 4 12B: A unified, encoder-free multimodal model
items.author: rvz
items.rawContent: Gemma 4 12B: A unified, encoder-free multimodal model
items.summary: Gemma 4 12B 是一种新型统一多模态模型，摒弃传统编码器设计，支持文本、图像等多模态输入，强调架构简化与端到端训练。该模型目前仅以研究公告形式披露，尚未开源或提供可用工具接口。
items.summaryEn: Gemma 4 12B is a novel unified multimodal model that eliminates separate encoders, enabling end-to-end training across modalities like text and images; it represents a conceptual and architectural advance but lacks released code, weights, or practical deployment guidance.
items.titleEn: Gemma 4 12B: A unified, encoder-free multimodal model

items.title: I built a vulnerable app and spent $1,500 seeing if LLMs could hack it
items.author: jc4p
items.rawContent: I built a vulnerable app and spent $1,500 seeing if LLMs could hack it
items.summary: 作者构建了一个存在安全漏洞的Web应用，并投入1500美元使用主流大语言模型（如Claude、GPT-4）尝试自动化渗透测试，探讨LLM在真实红队任务中的能力边界与局限性。
items.summaryEn: The author built a deliberately vulnerable web application and spent $1,500 testing whether LLMs (e.g., Claude, GPT-4) could autonomously discover and exploit real-world security flaws—assessing their practical utility and limitations in offensive security tasks.
items.titleEn: I built a vulnerable app and spent $1,500 seeing if LLMs could hack it

items.title: Uber's $1,500/month AI limit is a useful signal for AI tool pricing
items.author: pdyc
items.rawContent: https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-06-02/uber-caps... (https://archive.ph/ZrwAy)
items.summary: 本文讨论优步对AI工具（如Claude Code）设置每月1500美元使用上限的商业决策，将其视为AI企业服务定价趋势的重要信号，反映大公司对AI成本管控的现实考量。
items.summaryEn: This piece analyzes Uber's imposition of a $1,500/month cap on AI tool usage (e.g., Claude Code) as a strategic cost-control measure and interprets it as an indicative signal for broader AI enterprise pricing trends.
items.titleEn: Uber's $1,500/month AI limit is a useful signal for AI tool pricing

items.title: Show HN: Uruky (EU-based Kagi alternative) now has Image Search and URL Rewrites

For the source code sharing, we've talked with lawyers and are inclined to no longer require the NDA/NCC for privacy reasons shared with us before (signing requires identification), but instead use a source-available permissive

items.title: Do Text Edits Generalize to Visual Generation? Benchmarking Cross-Modal Knowledge Editing in UMMs
items.author: Xin Gao
items.rawContent: Unified multimodal models (UMMs) have emerged as a promising paradigm for general-purpose multimodal intelligence. As they are deployed in real-world applications, effectively updating internal knowledge becomes critical. While knowledge editing has matured for text-only models, it remains unclear whether edits that successfully modify textual outputs also transfer to image generation in UMMs. To study this question, we introduce UniKE, the first benchmark for cross-modality knowledge editing in
items.summary: 本文提出UniKE基准，首次系统评估统一多模态模型（UMMs）中跨模态知识编辑的有效性，探究文本层面的知识修改能否泛化至图像生成任务。
items.summaryEn: This paper introduces UniKE, the first benchmark for evaluating cross-modal knowledge editing in unified multimodal models (UMMs), investigating whether knowledge edits applied to text outputs generalize to visual generation.
items.titleEn: Do Text Edits Generalize to Visual Generation? Benchmarking Cross-Modal Knowledge Editing in UMMs

items.title: Reproducing, Analyzing, and Detecting Reward Hacking in Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning
items.author: Xuekang Wang
items.rawContent: Rubric-based reinforcement learning (RL) uses an LLM-as-a-Judge (LaaJ) to score model outputs according to rubrics as rewards. However, policy models may exploit latent biases in the judge, leading to reward hacking and ineffective or unsafe training outcomes. In real-world rubric-based RL, such hacking behaviors are often subtle and entangled with multiple judge biases, making them difficult to analyze, detect, and mitigate. In this paper, we introduce CHERRL, a controllable hacking environment
items.summary: 本文提出CHERRL——一个可控的奖励黑客环境，用于复现、分析和检测基于评分标准的强化学习中由LLM裁判引发的奖励黑客行为，并系统研究其成因与缓解路径。
items.summaryEn: This paper introduces CHERRL, a controllable hacking environment to reproduce, analyze, and detect reward hacking in rubric-based reinforcement learning—where LLM-as-a-Judge biases are exploited by policy models—offering systematic insights into causes, detection, and mitigation.
items.titleEn: Reproducing, Analyzing, and Detecting Reward Hacking in Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning

items.title: Benchmarks are Not Enough: RAMP for Runtime Assessing of Agentic Models in Production Systems
items.author: Yipeng Ouyang
items.rawContent: LLM agents are rapidly evolving from coding assistants into autonomous software engineering systems. However, existing evaluation methodologies remain largely centered on static, isolated, and short-horizon benchmarks that fail to capture the dynamic complexity of real-world production workflows. As a result, benchmark performance may poorly reflect practical capability under realistic runtime environments involving long execution chains, tool interactions, dependency management, and iterative f
items.summary: 本文提出RAMP评估框架，旨在弥补现有静态基准测试的不足，针对生产环境中智能体模型（如LLM Agent）的动态运行时行为（如长链执行、工具调用、依赖管理）进行真实场景化评估。
items.summaryEn: This paper introduces RAMP, a runtime assessment framework designed to address the limitations of static, isolated benchmarks by evaluating agentic LLMs under realistic production conditions—including long-horizon execution, tool interaction, dependency management, and iterative feedback.
items.titleEn: Benchmarks are Not Enough: RAMP for Runtime Assessing of Agentic Models in Production Systems

items.title: OVO-S-Bench: A Hierarchical Benchmark for Streaming Spatial Intelligence in Multimodal LLMs
items.author: Yifei Li
items.rawContent: Multimodal agents in robotics, AR, and autonomous driving must reason about places and layouts from continuous egocentric streams, often using evidence outside the current view. Existing benchmarks either evaluate offline over full videos or target events rather than spatial structure. We introduce OVO-S-Bench, a fully human-annotated benchmark for streaming spatial intelligence, comprising 1,680 questions over 348 source videos. Annotation involves 12 trained annotators, each also serving as a
items.summary: OVO-S-Bench 是一个全新的人工标注分层基准，专为评估多模态大语言模型在连续第一人称视频流中进行空间智能推理（如布局理解、跨视角空间推断）的能力而设计，填补了现有基准在流式空间认知评估上的空白。
items.summaryEn: OVO-S-Bench is a novel, fully human-annotated hierarchical benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal LLMs’ streaming spatial intelligence—such as layout reasoning and cross-frame spatial inference—from continuous egocentric video streams, addressing a critical gap in existing evaluation frameworks.
items.titleEn: OVO-S-Bench: A Hierarchical Benchmark for Streaming Spatial Intelligence in Multimodal LLMs

items.title: OpenSTBench: Beyond Semantic Evaluation for Speech Translation
items.author: Yanjie An
items.rawContent: Speech translation systems increasingly span speech-to-text translation (S2TT), speech-to-speech translation (S2ST), offline translation, and streaming generation, producing outputs that differ in modality, speech realization, and timing behavior. Existing evaluation practices assess important aspects such as translation quality, speech quality, and temporal quality, but these aspects are often evaluated under separate protocols, making it difficult to compare heterogeneous systems comprehensive
items.summary: OpenSTBench 是一项面向语音翻译（ST）系统的新型综合评估基准，旨在统一评估跨模态（S2TT/S2ST）、离线/流式系统在翻译质量、语音质量和时序质量等方面的性能。该工作指出当前评估协议割裂、难以横向比较异构系统的问题，并提出标准化评测框架。
items.summaryEn: OpenSTBench is a novel comprehensive benchmark for speech translation (ST) systems, designed to unify evaluation across modalities (S2TT/S2ST), offline/streaming paradigms, and dimensions including translation quality, speech quality, and temporal quality. It addresses the fragmentation of current evaluation protocols and proposes a standardized framework for fair comparison of heterogeneous ST systems.
items.titleEn: OpenSTBench: Beyond Semantic Evaluation for Speech Translation

items.title: Economy of Minds: Emerging Multi-Agent Intelligence with Economic Interactions
items.author: Zhenting Qi
items.rawContent: How can a population of agents self-orchestrate and self-adapt into stronger collective intelligence without centralized control? Inspired by Friedrich Hayek's economic theory of decentralized coordination in markets, we study this question through an agent economy in which agents compete via auctions for the right to act, exchange payments, and accumulate wealth from environmental rewards. These simple economic signals induce decentralized credit assignment, driving planning without global orch
items.summary: 该研究受哈耶克经济思想启发，提出一种基于拍卖、支付与财富积累的多智能体经济框架，通过去中心化经济信号实现智能体群体的自组织与协同规划。
items.summaryEn: Inspired by Friedrich Hayek’s economic theory, this work proposes an agent economy—featuring auctions, payments, and wealth accumulation—to enable decentralized, self-organizing multi-agent intelligence without centralized control.
items.titleEn: Economy of Minds: Emerging Multi-Agent Intelligence with Economic Interactions

items.title: Filter, Then Reweight: Rethinking Optimization Granularity in On-Policy Distillation
items.author: Yuying Li
items.rawContent: On-Policy distillation (OPD) in large language models is shifting from full-trace KL supervision toward more selective training paradigms. Recent OPD methods increasingly focus on selecting which trajectories to learn from, which tokens are most informative, and which supervision signals are most reliable. Motivated by this trend, we rethink optimization granularity of OPD and propose \fireicon\ FiRe-OPD (Filter, then Reweight), which jointly adjusts supervision signals at both trajectory and to
items.summary: 本文提出FiRe-OPD方法，通过先过滤再重加权的两阶段策略，重新思考在线策略蒸馏（OPD）中的优化粒度问题，聚焦于轨迹和token层面的监督信号选择与校准。
items.summaryEn: This paper proposes FiRe-OPD (Filter, then Reweight), a novel two-stage framework that rethinks optimization granularity in on-policy distillation by jointly filtering and reweighting supervision signals at both trajectory and token levels.
items.titleEn: Filter, Then Reweight: Rethinking Optimization Granularity in On-Policy Distillation

items.title: SpatialAct: Probing Spatial Reasoning-to-Action Capabilities of VLM Agents in 3D Scenes
items.author: Tianhui Liu
items.rawContent: Humans can effortlessly perceive spatial layouts, form cognitive representations, reason about spatial relations, and translate such reasoning into actions in everyday 3D environments. Although recent vision-language models (VLMs) have shown promising performance on observation-conditioned spatial perception and reasoning tasks, it remains unclear whether they can build coherent spatial understanding, act upon it, and refine their actions through multi-turn feedback. To study this problem, we in
items.summary: 该研究提出SpatialAct基准，用于系统评估多模态大模型（VLM）在3D场景中从空间推理到具身动作执行的端到端能力，填补了现有评测在空间理解—行动闭环上的空白。
items.summaryEn: This work introduces SpatialAct, a new benchmark designed to systematically evaluate the end-to-end spatial reasoning-to-action capabilities of vision-language models (VLMs) in 3D environments—assessing not just perception and reasoning, but also action execution and iterative refinement via multi-turn feedback.
items.titleEn: SpatialAct: Probing Spatial Reasoning-to-Action Capabilities of VLM Agents in 3D Scenes

items.title: Deep Embedded Multiplicative DMD for Algebra-Preserving Koopman Learning
items.author: Kelan Gray
items.rawContent: Koopman theory turns nonlinear dynamics into a linear spectral problem. In computation, however, everything depends on a hard finite-dimensional choice: the observables must be expressive, nearly invariant under the dynamics, and, ideally, compatible with composition. Deep Koopman methods learn flexible coordinates, whereas structure-preserving methods enforce operator identities on fixed dictionaries. We combine these ideas by introducing Deep Embedded Multiplicative Dynamic Mode Decomposition
items.summary: 该研究提出了一种深度嵌入式乘性动态模态分解（DMD）方法，旨在实现代数结构保持的Koopman算子学习，兼顾表达性与动力学不变性。工作属于理论驱动的AI建模范式创新，聚焦于可解释动力系统建模。
items.summaryEn: This paper introduces Deep Embedded Multiplicative DMD, a novel Koopman learning framework that jointly optimizes for expressivity, dynamical invariance, and algebraic structure preservation (e.g., compositionality). It bridges deep representation learning with physics-informed operator constraints.
items.titleEn: Deep Embedded Multiplicative DMD for Algebra-Preserving Koopman Learning

items.title: Unlocking Feature Learning in Gated Delta Networks at Scale
items.author: Yifeng Liu
items.rawContent: Training and scaling Large Language Models demand enormous computational resources, motivating both efficient sub-quadratic architectures and principled hyperparameter tuning methods. While the Maximal Update Parametrization (μP) has enabled zero-shot hyperparameter transfer for standard Transformers, its extension to linear models, particularly those with structured state transitions and complicated architectures, remains largely unexplored. By rigorously propagating coordinate-size estimates t
items.summary: 本文探讨了在门控Delta网络（Gated Delta Networks）中规模化实现特征学习的理论基础，重点扩展Maximal Update Parametrization（μP）方法以支持具有结构化状态转移的非标准架构。研究涉及坐标尺度传播与超参数可迁移性，属于前沿AI模型训练理论。
items.summaryEn: This paper investigates principled feature learning in Gated Delta Networks at scale, extending the Maximal Update Parametrization (μP) framework to non-standard architectures with structured state transitions. It provides theoretical analysis of coordinate-wise scaling and zero-shot hyperparameter transfer beyond standard Transformers.
items.titleEn: Unlocking Feature Learning in Gated Delta Networks at Scale
